analysis.notEnoughSpeech: Not enough speech detected. Speak louder or closer, or check the selected input.

check.vsReference: {{dev, number(minimumFractionDigits: 1; maximumFractionDigits: 1; signDisplay: exceptZero)}} dB vs reference

level.title: Speech level
level.good: Comfortable level for calls and streams.
level.quiet: Voice is quiet; listeners will turn you up, raising noise too.
level.hot: Voice is hot; risk of distortion and listener fatigue.
level.fixQuiet: Raise compressor makeup gain (ReaComp wet) 3–6 dB, or Wave XLR gain a few dB.
level.fixHot: Lower Wave XLR gain or compressor makeup by 3–6 dB.

peaks.title: Peaks / clipping
peaks.value: peak {{peak, number(minimumFractionDigits: 1; maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dBFS · {{clip}} clipped samples
peaks.bad: Peaks hit the ceiling and will crackle.
peaks.fix: Lower gain 2–3 dB; keep ReaComp 'Limit output' on.

noise.title: Background noise
noise.value: {{noise, number(minimumFractionDigits: 1; maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dBFS in silence · SNR {{snr, number(maximumFractionDigits: 0)}} dB
noise.bad: Hiss, fans or room noise are audible in pauses.
noise.roughGood: No clean 3 s silence found; estimate is rough. Pauses are clean.
noise.roughBad: No clean 3 s silence found; estimate is rough. Hiss, fans or room noise are audible in pauses.
noise.fix: Move away from PC fans, lower gain and speak closer, or tighten ReaGate threshold.

overprocessed.title: Over-processing
overprocessed.value: {{zero, number(maximumFractionDigits: 0)}} % digital silence · {{switches, number(maximumFractionDigits: 0)}} cuts per 10 s
overprocessed.good: Noise removal and the gate leave your voice alone.
overprocessed.bad: Parts of the take are cut to total silence and the sound keeps switching on and off, so words get chopped.
overprocessed.fix: Noise removal or the gate is too strong and is cutting your voice — reduce it.

silence.title: Silence window
silence.detail: Something loud happened during the 3 s silence, so the noise reading may be off.
silence.fix: Re-record and stay fully silent until the status says 'Read now'.

hum.title: Mains hum
hum.value: strongest {{hz}} Hz, +{{db, number(minimumFractionDigits: 1; maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB over neighbours
hum.gated: Pauses are silent, but the {{hz}} Hz hum is still there under your voice while you talk (the gate only hides it in pauses).
hum.bad: A steady {{hz}} Hz buzz from the power line sits under your voice.
hum.fix: Ground loop: try another USB port (rear, on the motherboard), unplug chargers on the same strip, keep XLR cable away from power bricks. ReaGate hides it in pauses only.

tones.title: Fan / machine tones
tones.value2: {{hz1}} Hz +{{db1, number(maximumFractionDigits: 0)}} dB, {{hz2}} Hz +{{db2, number(maximumFractionDigits: 0)}} dB
tones.value3: {{hz1}} Hz +{{db1, number(maximumFractionDigits: 0)}} dB, {{hz2}} Hz +{{db2, number(maximumFractionDigits: 0)}} dB, {{hz3}} Hz +{{db3, number(maximumFractionDigits: 0)}} dB
tones.good: No strong steady tones in pauses.
tones.bad: Steady tones from fans, servers or other machines sit under your voice.
tones.fix: Turn the mic so its least sensitive side faces the machine; the suggested settings add narrow EQ notches at these tones.

bandsnr.title: Voice vs room (per band)
bandsnr.value: voice bands {{v, number(maximumFractionDigits: 0)}} dB over the room
bandsnr.good: Your voice is well above the room noise where clarity lives (640 Hz–5 kHz).
bandsnr.warn: The room noise is close to your voice where clarity lives (640 Hz–5 kHz).
bandsnr.bad: The room noise competes with your voice where clarity lives (640 Hz–5 kHz).
bandsnr.fix: Speak closer and keep the noise off-axis, then use the noise-reduction step in the suggested settings.

rumble.title: Rumble (40–80 Hz)
rumble.bad: Desk thumps, footsteps and AC rumble muddy the signal.
rumble.fix: Keep Wave XLR Lowcut on (try 120 Hz); use a boom arm or shock mount so desk bumps don't reach the mic.

boom.title: Boom (80–160 Hz)
boom.good: Bass is in a healthy range.
boom.high: Too much bass, usually proximity effect from being very close to a dynamic mic.
boom.low: Voice is thin in the bass.
boom.fixHigh: Back off 2–3 cm from the mic, or set ReaEQ low shelf at 150 Hz to -4/-5 dB.
boom.fixLow: Move 2 cm closer, or reduce the 150 Hz low shelf cut.

warmth.title: Warmth (160–320 Hz)
warmth.high: Low-mid buildup makes the voice thick and muffled.
warmth.low: Voice lacks warmth and may sound thin.
warmth.fixHigh: ReaEQ: cut around 250 Hz by 3–4 dB, bandwidth ~1.5.
warmth.fixLow: Reduce the 300 Hz cut to -2 dB.

mud.title: Mud / boxiness (320–640 Hz)
mud.good: Low-mids are not masking your consonants.
mud.high: Boxy, cardboard sound that hides consonants; a top cause of 'not clear'.
mud.low: Low-mids are scooped; voice can sound hollow.
mud.fixHigh: ReaEQ: cut 400–500 Hz by 3–4 dB, bandwidth ~1.2.
mud.fixLow: Reduce the 300 Hz cut, or move it lower (200 Hz).

body.title: Body (640 Hz–1.25 kHz)
body.good: Core of the voice is solid.
body.low: The core of the voice is scooped out; lows and highs dominate, so it sounds hollow and distant.
body.fixHigh: ReaEQ: cut ~900 Hz by 2–3 dB, bandwidth ~1.
body.fixLow: ReaEQ: add +2/+3 dB at ~1 kHz, bandwidth ~1.5, and ease back the low shelf and highs.

definition.title: Definition (1.25–2.5 kHz)
definition.good: Vowel and consonant definition is fine.

presence.title: Presence (2.5–5 kHz)
presence.high: Upper mids are pushed; can sound harsh or tiring.
presence.low: Voice sounds dull and distant; this band carries clarity.
presence.fixHigh: Lower the 4 kHz boost by 2–3 dB.
presence.fixLow: Raise the 4 kHz band to +4/+5 dB, and speak on-axis, straight into the capsule.

sibilance.title: Sibilance (5–10 kHz)
sibilance.good: S and T sounds are balanced.
sibilance.high: S sounds are sharp and can hiss.
sibilance.fixHigh: Turn on Elgato De-Esser, or lower the 10 kHz high shelf 2 dB; angle the mic slightly off your mouth.
sibilance.fixLow: Raise the 10 kHz high shelf to +4 dB.

air.title: Air (10–16 kHz)
air.high: Lots of top end; can sound brittle or hissy.
air.low: Very little top end. Common for budget dynamic mics.
air.fixHigh: Lower the 10 kHz high shelf 2 dB.
air.fixLow: ReaEQ high shelf at 10 kHz +3 to +5 dB (watch sibilance).

harsh.title: Harsh S peaks
harsh.detail: Individual S sounds spike hard even if the average is fine.
harsh.fix: Turn on Elgato De-Esser (light setting) after the EQ.

consistency.title: Consistency
consistency.value: {{v, number(minimumFractionDigits: 1; maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB spread between seconds
consistency.bad: Level jumps between phrases; listeners will ride the volume.
consistency.fix: Keep the same distance (a fist away) and lower ReaComp threshold 3 dB.

failure.silent: We only got silence. This input isn't hearing your mic. Press Change and pick another input, or check that your audio app sends your mic to it.
failure.tooQuiet: Your voice barely reached the mic. Turn up the input volume (gain) on your mic or audio interface, or check that you picked the right input.
failure.noisyPause: The quiet part was almost as loud as your reading. Stay silent until the countdown ends, and pause anything else that plays sound into this input, like music or a call.
failure.tooShort: Your volume looks fine, but there wasn't enough talking. Read the whole text after the countdown and keep going until the end.

address.end: Speak straight into the top of the mic.
address.side: Speak into the front side of the mic (usually where the logo is), not the top.
address.unknown: Point the capsule at your mouth.

placement.cardioid: Point the back of the mic at the loudest noise source (fan, PC, server).
placement.supercardioid: Keep the loudest noise at the mic's sides, about 125° off-axis.
placement.other: Move the mic closer to you and away from the noise; this pickup pattern won't reject it.

suggest.gainQuiet: The raw take is quiet ({{speech, number(maximumFractionDigits: 0)}} dBFS). Raise the Wave XLR gain about {{db}} dB first, then record the control takes again. The gate and compressor values depend on it.
suggest.gainHot: The raw take is hot ({{speech, number(maximumFractionDigits: 0)}} dBFS). Lower the Wave XLR gain about {{db}} dB and record the control takes again.
suggest.noisy: The input is noisy: the room/input noise ({{noise, number(maximumFractionDigits: 0)}} dBFS) is only {{snr, number(maximumFractionDigits: 0)}} dB under your voice. No gate or EQ setting can separate them, and the gate would cut quiet words. Get the most out of the room:
suggest.noisyNext: Speak closer and switch off what you can, then set up the noise-reduction step below before the EQ. Re-record the control takes to check: the closer to 30 dB, the cleaner.
suggest.condenser: Condenser mics pick up more of the room: stay closer and lower the gain.
